title:
IgG4-Related Disease May Be a Tumor-like 
Condition—Diagnostic and Therapeutic Approach
content: Background: IgG4-RD is an autoimmune fibro-inflammatory condition with chronic evolution and systemic involvement. The incidence is not clearly established. IgG4-RD can easily mimic other pathologic conditions, such as tumors and infections; therefore, affected patients are frequently misdiagnosed and sometimes undertreated. The disease can affect multiple organs and needs a multidisciplinary therapeutic approach. Sometimes, the lack of diagnosis is a result of the high cost of dedicated serological analyses, as well as patient non-compliance. Methods: This review summarizes the current state of knowledge regarding the diagnosis and treatment of IgG4-RD, together with the authors’ practical experience. Results: The diagnosis of IgG4-RD has no specific clinical, paraclinical, or imaging aspects. This condition can mimic any other disease in the affected organ. Frequently, a diagnosis will result from the exclusion of other diseases and even the analysis of a patient’s reaction to a dedicated treatment. Spontaneous remission is rarely observed, and recurrence is common . Most patients have a favorable response to glucocorticoid therapy, but there is a need for maintenance treatment due to the risk of recurrence. Conclusions: IgG4-RD is an underdiagnosed and undertreated condition due to the lack of specific clinical, paraclinical, and imaging changes, the cost-related limitations of dedicated laboratory analyses, and patient non-compliance. If, in the case of patients with fibro-inflammatory changes in one or more structures, the diagnosis of IgG4-RD is excluded, even by elimination, the complications of its occurrence are prevented. This approach is cost-effective, as it prevents complications that require acute and long-term supportive treatment.
